properties.name: `reflow2 read` and `reflow2 write`: the --call door with the read/write split in the command text, so one terminal rule (`^reflow2 read `) approves every read and no write (door plan step 3)
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Two verbs on the reflow2-mcp binary, reached unchanged through the installer's `reflow2` command. `read <tool> [JSON]` runs a tool only when its served read_only_hint says it reads and, for export_graph and export_surface, no `path` is given (item 1's file rule, now one function, service::writes_a_file, shared with the --read-only client). Every other tool is refused by name before anything is opened, exit 1, naming `reflow2 write <tool>`, and what `read` accepts runs as `--read-only --call`. `write <tool> [JSON]` is `--call`. `read --list` prints the split from the served annotations (78 read and 117 write of 195). Only the tool, its JSON (positional, --args, or - for stdin) and --graph-path may follow a verb, and the one-shot table has a row for each verb. Both verbs log errors only. MERGE TRAIN (#662, #663, #665, #666, 2026-10-03): #661 had merged first, so a writing --call keeps the committed export current; `write` is --call, so its row in the one-shot table also honours --export-to and --no-export (typed before the verb: `reflow2 --no-export write ...`), and `read`, which writes nothing, still refuses both by name.
